consensus_summary: Blind responses converge on lamp oil primarily symbolizing the Holy Spirit (indwelling presence/power sustaining light, witness, and readiness), especially via Matt 25 and Zech 4 plus anointing texts; common alternatives are preparedness/watchfulness, good works/obedience, or nontransferable faith/grace (with minority notes of joy or Word).
book_summary: Spirit-taught truth and correction received, kept, and worked into proven obedience—the tested, pressed fruit of the Spirit stored inwardly; light is that obedience made visible as an example to others.
rationale: The book’s claim is compatible with the consensus Holy-Spirit core (as Spirit-enabled fruit producing obedience) and with the frequent alternatives of good works or inward grace/readiness, yet it materially sharpens and narrows them into a precise composite—truth/correction (drawn from reproof and ‘buy the truth’ texts) stored as pressed fruit that yields visible works—rather than equating oil simply with the Spirit himself or with generic preparedness.
strongest_objection: Traditional and popular readings treat lamp oil (especially Matt 25) as the Holy Spirit or simple readiness, not a constructed synthesis of ‘Spirit-taught truth and correction’; combining lamp-oil, reproof-oil, and anointing-oil metaphors risks over-allegorization not required by any single text.
